annotation.title_clean: Ethics in autonomous robots as philosophy in silico: The study case of phronetic machine ethics
annotation.title_en: Ethics in autonomous robots as philosophy in silico: The study case of phronetic machine ethics
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical paper proposing in silico computational modeling as a method for philosophy and ethics, using Aristotelian phronesis-based machine ethics for autonomous robots as a case study. It argues modeling forces precise concept definitions and may help develop ethical robots and clarify ethical problems. It contains no regulatory content.
key_provisions_or_claims: In silico modeling can be a methodological tool for philosophy, including ethics.
Phronetic decisions are case-specific, non-procedural and intuitive, which makes them hard to encode in robots.
Computer models demand precise definitions, exposing ambiguities in ethical concepts.
Modeling may aid development of ethical autonomous robots and deepen insight into ethics.
